requirements.title: Do not convey IP header fields
requirements.statement: These mechanisms MUST NOT convey fields of the IP header.

requirements.title: Do not tunnel other IP protocols
requirements.statement: These mechanisms MUST NOT tunnel other IP protocols.

requirements.title: Use QUIC variable-length integer encoding
requirements.statement: This specification MUST use the variable-length integer encoding from Section 16 of [QUIC].

requirements.title: Allow non-minimal variable-length integer encodings
requirements.statement: Variable-length integer values MAY be encoded in more than the minimum number of bytes necessary.

requirements.title: Interpret stream as connection without multiplexing
requirements.statement: When the HTTP version in use does not support multiplexing streams (such as HTTP/1.1), any reference to "stream" in this document MUST represent the entire connection.

requirements.title: Limit URI Template level to 3 or lower
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST be a level 3 template or lower.

requirements.title: Require absolute-form URI Template
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST be in absolute form.

requirements.title: Require non-empty URI Template components
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST include non-empty scheme, authority, and path components.

requirements.title: Require a leading slash in the path component
requirements.statement: The path component of a URI Template MUST start with a slash "/".

requirements.title: Restrict template variables to the path or query components
requirements.statement: All template variables MUST be within the path or query components of the URI.

requirements.title: Allow other URI Template variables
requirements.statement: The URI Template MAY contain other variables.

requirements.title: Allow target and ipproto variables
requirements.statement: The URI Template MAY contain the variables "target" and "ipproto".

requirements.title: Require non-empty target and ipproto values
requirements.statement: If the "target" or "ipproto" variables are included, their values MUST NOT be empty.

requirements.title: Restrict URI Template characters to printable ASCII
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST contain only ASCII characters in the range 0x21-0x7E inclusive, with percent-encoding allowed.

requirements.title: Forbid dot-prefix label expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Label Expansion with Dot-Prefix.

requirements.title: Forbid fragment expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Fragment Expansion ("#" operator).

requirements.title: Forbid reserved expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Reserved Expansion ("+" operator).

requirements.title: Forbid semicolon-prefix path-style parameter expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Path-Style Parameter Expansion with Semicolon-Prefix.

requirements.title: Forbid slash-prefix path segment expansion
requirements.statement: The URI Template MUST NOT use Path Segment Expansion with Slash-Prefix.

requirements.title: Allow general-purpose URI Template implementations
requirements.statement: Clients MAY use a general-purpose URI Template implementation that lacks this specific validation.

requirements.title: Recommend validating the requirements above
requirements.statement: Clients SHOULD validate the requirements above.

requirements.title: Reject invalid URI Template configurations
requirements.statement: If a client detects that any of the requirements above are not met by a URI Template, the client MUST reject its configuration and abort the request without sending it to the IP proxy.

requirements.title: Allow use of the default template for limited clients
requirements.statement: Clients with such limitations MAY attempt to access IP proxying capabilities using the default template, defined as "https://$PROXY_HOST:$PROXY_PORT/.well-known/masque/ip/{target}/{ipproto}/".

requirements.title: Recommend service at the default template location
requirements.statement: IP proxy deployments SHOULD offer service at this location if they need to interoperate with such clients.

requirements.title: Initiate IP tunnel requests with connect-ip
requirements.statement: A client MUST issue a request containing the `connect-ip` upgrade token to initiate an IP tunnel associated with a single HTTP stream.

requirements.title: Expand URI templates for IP proxying requests
requirements.statement: When sending its IP proxying request, the client SHALL perform URI Template expansion to determine the path and query of its request.

requirements.title: Protect IP proxying over HTTP with encryption
requirements.statement: IP proxying over HTTP MUST be operated over TLS or QUIC encryption, or another equivalent encryption protocol, to provide confidentiality, integrity, and authentication.

requirements.title: Forward requests to the configured HTTP server
requirements.statement: If the recipient is configured to use another HTTP server, it MUST forward the request to that server.

requirements.title: Act as an IP proxy otherwise
requirements.statement: Otherwise, the recipient MUST act as an IP proxy.

requirements.title: Allow rejection of IP proxying requests
requirements.statement: An IP proxy MAY reject the IP proxying request.

requirements.title: Extract tunnel variables from the reconstructed URI
requirements.statement: An IP proxy MUST extract the optional `target` and `ipproto` variables from the reconstructed URI, decode their percent-encoding, and establish an IP tunnel.

requirements.title: Treat invalid tunnel variables as malformed
requirements.statement: If the decoded `target` or `ipproto` variables fail validation, the IP proxy MUST treat the request as malformed.

requirements.title: Validate decoded tunnel variables
requirements.statement: IP proxies MUST validate the decoded `target` and `ipproto` variables against Section 4.6.

requirements.title: Resolve DNS names before replying
requirements.statement: If the `target` variable is a DNS name, the IP proxy MUST resolve it to IPv4 and/or IPv6 addresses via A and/or AAAA records before replying to the HTTP request.

requirements.title: Reject requests when processing errors occur
requirements.statement: If errors occur during this process, the IP proxy MUST reject the request.

requirements.title: Report proxy errors with Proxy-Status details
requirements.statement: If errors occur during this process, the IP proxy SHOULD send details using an appropriate Proxy-Status header field.

requirements.title: Tie tunnel lifetime to request stream
requirements.statement: The lifetime of the IP forwarding tunnel MUST be tied to the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Maintain tunnel assignments while the request stream is open
requirements.statement: The IP proxy MUST maintain all IP address and route assignments associated with the IP forwarding tunnel while the request stream is open.

requirements.title: Allow tunnel teardown for inactivity
requirements.statement: IP proxies MAY tear down the tunnel due to inactivity.

requirements.title: Close the request stream when tearing down the tunnel
requirements.statement: If an IP proxy tears down the tunnel due to inactivity, it MUST close the request stream.

requirements.title: Abort the request on a non-successful proxying response
requirements.statement: If the client receives any response other than a successful IP proxying response, the client MUST abort the request.

requirements.title: Use GET method
requirements.statement: The method SHALL be "GET".

requirements.title: Include the Host header field
requirements.statement: The request SHALL include a single Host header field containing the host and optional port of the IP proxy.

requirements.title: Include a Connection header with Upgrade
requirements.statement: The request SHALL include a Connection header field with value "Upgrade"; matching is case-insensitive.

requirements.title: Include the Upgrade header field
requirements.statement: The request SHALL include an Upgrade header field with value "connect-ip".

requirements.title: Respond to malformed requests with an error
requirements.statement: The recipient of such a malformed request MUST respond with an error.

requirements.title: Use 400 for malformed requests
requirements.statement: The recipient of such a malformed request SHOULD use the 400 (Bad Request) status code.

requirements.title: HTTP response status code is 101
requirements.statement: The HTTP status code on the response SHALL be 101 (Switching Protocols).

requirements.title: Connection header value is Upgrade
requirements.statement: The response SHALL include a Connection header field with value "Upgrade"; the value comparison is case-insensitive.

requirements.title: Upgrade header value is connect-ip
requirements.statement: The response SHALL include a single Upgrade header field with value "connect-ip".

requirements.title: Response meets Capsule Protocol start requirements
requirements.statement: The response SHALL meet the requirements of HTTP responses that start the Capsule Protocol; see Section 3.2 of [HTTP-DGRAM].

requirements.title: Failed proxying attempt closes connection
requirements.statement: If any of these requirements are not met, the client MUST treat this proxying attempt as failed and close the connection.

requirements.title: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 IP proxying uses Extended CONNECT
requirements.statement: When using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, IP proxying requests MUST use HTTP Extended CONNECT.
notes: Normalized the descriptive RFC wording into a testable requirement.

requirements.title: Servers send an HTTP Setting
requirements.statement: Servers MUST send an HTTP Setting, as specified in [EXT-CONNECT2] and [EXT-CONNECT3].

requirements.title: Method pseudo-header is CONNECT
requirements.statement: The :method pseudo-header field SHALL be "CONNECT".

requirements.title: Protocol pseudo-header is connect-ip
requirements.statement: The :protocol pseudo-header field SHALL be "connect-ip".

requirements.title: Authority pseudo-header contains proxy authority
requirements.statement: The :authority pseudo-header field SHALL contain the authority of the IP proxy.

requirements.title: Path pseudo-header is not empty
requirements.statement: The :path pseudo-header field SHALL NOT be empty.

requirements.title: Scheme pseudo-header is not empty
requirements.statement: The :scheme pseudo-header field SHALL NOT be empty.

requirements.title: URI Template values contain scheme and path
requirements.statement: The values MUST contain the scheme and path from the URI Template after the URI Template expansion process has been completed.

requirements.title: Nonconforming IP proxying request is malformed
requirements.statement: An IP proxying request that does not conform to these restrictions MUST be treated as malformed.

requirements.title: Response status code is 2xx
requirements.statement: The HTTP status code on the response MUST be in the 2xx (Successful) range.

requirements.title: Response meets Capsule Protocol HTTP requirements
requirements.statement: The response MUST meet the requirements of HTTP responses that start the Capsule Protocol.

requirements.title: Failed proxying attempts are aborted
requirements.statement: If any of these requirements are not met, the client MUST treat this proxying attempt as failed and abort the request.

requirements.title: IP prefix targets support only one IP version
requirements.statement: If `target` is an IP prefix, the request MUST use only a single IP version.

requirements.title: IP proxy sends scoped route advertisement
requirements.statement: The IP proxy SHOULD send a ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule that includes routes for all addresses that were resolved for the requested hostname, that are accessible to the IP proxy, and belong to an address family for which the IP proxy also sends an Assigned Address.

requirements.title: Scope proxying to a specific IP protocol
requirements.statement: If present, `ipproto` MUST specify a specific IP protocol for this request.

requirements.title: Wildcard or absent ipproto means any protocol
requirements.statement: If the value is `*` or the variable is omitted, the client MUST request any IP protocol.

requirements.title: Define ipproto as allowable next-header value
requirements.statement: The `ipproto` variable MUST indicate an allowable next-header value carried in the outermost IP headers of HTTP Datagrams.

requirements.title: Always allow ICMP traffic
requirements.statement: ICMP traffic MUST always be allowed, regardless of the `ipproto` value.

requirements.title: Conform target and ipproto to Figure 6 format
requirements.statement: Using the terms IPv6address, IPv4address, and reg-name from [URI], the `target` and `ipproto` variables MUST conform to the Figure 6 format using [ABNF] notation.

requirements.title: Percent-encode colons in IPv6 targets
requirements.statement: If `target` contains an IPv6 literal or prefix, its colons (":") MUST be percent-encoded.

requirements.title: Precede target prefix lengths with %2F
requirements.statement: If present, the IP prefix length in `target` SHALL be preceded by a percent-encoded slash ("/"): "%2F".

requirements.title: Constrain target prefix length to address bits
requirements.statement: The IP prefix length MUST represent a decimal integer between 0 and the length of the IP address in bits, inclusive.

requirements.title: Zero uncovered lower bits in scoped targets
requirements.statement: If `target` contains an IP prefix and the prefix length is strictly less than the length of the IP address in bits, the lower bits of the IP address that are not covered by the prefix length MUST all be set to 0.

requirements.title: Constrain ipproto to decimal 0-255 or wildcard
requirements.statement: `ipproto` MUST represent a decimal integer between 0 and 255 inclusive or the wildcard value `*`.

requirements.title: Define ipproto grammar alternatives
requirements.statement: The `ipproto` grammar MUST be `1*3DIGIT / "*"`.

requirements.title: Define target grammar alternatives
requirements.statement: The `target` grammar MUST be `IPv6prefix / IPv4prefix / reg-name / "*"`.

requirements.title: Optionally perform access control using client scope
requirements.statement: IP proxies MAY perform access control using the scoping information provided by the client, and if the client is not authorized to access any of the destinations included in the scope, the proxy can immediately reject the request.

requirements.title: Allow any number of new capsules
requirements.statement: Both endpoints MAY send any number of these new capsules.

requirements.title: Contain the full assigned prefix list
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_ASSIGN Capsule MUST contain the full list of IP prefixes currently assigned to the receiver.

requirements.title: Define ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule wire format
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_ASSIGN Capsule MUST have Type 0x01, Length, and Assigned Address fields in that order.

requirements.title: Contain zero or more Assigned Addresses
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_ASSIGN Capsule MUST contain a sequence of zero or more Assigned Addresses.

requirements.title: Define Assigned Address field layout and widths
requirements.statement: The Assigned Address structure MUST contain Request ID, IP Version (8 bits), IP Address (32 to 128 bits), and IP Prefix Length (8 bits) fields in that order.

requirements.title: Encode Request ID as variable-length integer
requirements.statement: Request ID MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: Set Request ID from Address Request context
requirements.statement: Request ID MUST contain the corresponding request field value when this address assignment is in response to an Address Request, and be zero otherwise.

requirements.title: IP Version field encoding
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: IP Version field meaning
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST identify the IP version of this address assignment.

requirements.title: Restrict IP Version to 4 or 6
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be either 4 or 6.

requirements.title: Set IP Address length by IP Version
requirements.statement: The IP Address field MUST be 32 bits when the IP Version field has value 4 and 128 bits when it has value 6.

requirements.title: IP Prefix Length field encoding
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: IP Prefix Length field meaning
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be the number of bits in the IP address used to define the prefix being assigned.

requirements.title: IP Prefix Length upper bound
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be less than or equal to the length of the IP Address field in bits.

requirements.title: Single-source-address permission at full-length prefix
requirements.statement: If the prefix length is equal to the length of the IP address, the receiver of this capsule MAY send packets from a single source address.

requirements.title: Prefix-scoped source-address permission
requirements.statement: If the prefix length is less than the length of the IP address, the receiver of this capsule MAY send packets from any source address that falls within the prefix.

requirements.title: Zero unused IP Address bits
requirements.statement: If the prefix length is strictly less than the length of the IP address in bits, the lower bits of the IP Address field that are not covered by the prefix length MUST all be set to 0.

requirements.title: Malformed capsule field handling
requirements.statement: If any of the capsule fields are malformed upon reception, the receiver of the capsule MUST follow the error-handling procedure defined in Section 3.3 of [HTTP-DGRAM].

requirements.title: Omitted address indicates removal
requirements.statement: If an ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule does not contain an address that was previously transmitted in another ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule, the receiver of the capsule MUST treat that address as removed.

requirements.title: Empty ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule removes all addresses
requirements.statement: If an ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule is empty, the receiver of the capsule MUST treat all addresses as removed.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST from an address-assignment expectation
requirements.statement: An endpoint that is expecting an address assignment MUST send an ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule, unless it does not need any address assignment.
notes: Sentence 4 was folded into the normalized requirement statement.

requirements.title: Unprompted ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsules
requirements.statement: Endpoints MAY send ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsules unprompted.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule length field
requirements.statement: The Length field MUST follow the Type field and be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule type
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_REQUEST Capsule Type field MUST be 0x02 and appear first.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST requested address field
requirements.statement: The Requested Address field MUST follow the Length field.

requirements.title: ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule contains one or more Requested Addresses
requirements.statement: The ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule MUST contain one or more Requested Address entries.

requirements.title: Requested Address IP Address field
requirements.statement: The IP Address field MUST appear third and be encoded as 32 to 128 bits.

requirements.title: Requested Address IP Prefix Length field
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST appear fourth and be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Requested Address IP Version field
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST appear second and be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Requested Address request ID field
requirements.statement: The Request ID field MUST appear first and be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: Encode Request ID as a variable-length integer
requirements.statement: The Request ID field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer.

requirements.title: Request ID reuse prohibition
requirements.statement: Request IDs MUST NOT be reused by an endpoint.

requirements.title: Request ID zero prohibition
requirements.statement: Request IDs MUST NOT be zero.

requirements.title: Encode IP Version as an 8-bit integer
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Limit IP Version values to 4 or 6
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be either 4 or 6.

requirements.title: Use 32-bit IP addresses for IPv4
requirements.statement: If the IP Version field has value 4, the IP Address field SHALL have a length of 32 bits.

requirements.title: Use 128-bit IP addresses for IPv6
requirements.statement: If the IP Version field has value 6, the IP Address field SHALL have a length of 128 bits.

requirements.title: Encode IP Prefix Length as an 8-bit integer
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Bound prefix length by address length
requirements.statement: The IP Prefix Length field MUST be less than or equal to the length of the IP Address field in bits.

requirements.title: Zero unused address bits beyond the prefix
requirements.statement: If the prefix length is strictly less than the length of the IP address in bits, the lower bits of the IP Address field that are not covered by the prefix length MUST all be set to 0.

requirements.title: Handle malformed capsule fields
requirements.statement: If any of the capsule fields are malformed upon reception, the receiver of the capsule MUST follow the error-handling procedure defined in Section 3.3 of [HTTP-DGRAM].

requirements.title: Assign addresses and send address assignment
requirements.statement: Upon receiving the ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule, an endpoint SHOULD assign one or more IP addresses to its peer and then respond with an ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsule to inform the peer of the assignment.

requirements.title: Match request IDs in assigned addresses
requirements.statement: For each Requested Address, the receiver of the ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule SHALL respond with an Assigned Address with a matching Request ID.

requirements.title: Set assigned values in assigned address responses
requirements.statement: If the requested address was assigned, the IP Address and IP Prefix Length fields in the Assigned Address response SHALL be set to the assigned values.

requirements.title: Encode unassigned addresses with zero values
requirements.statement: If the requested address was not assigned, the IP address and IP Prefix Length in the Assigned Address response SHALL be set to all-zero and the maximum length (0.0.0.0/32 or ::/128), respectively, to indicate that no address was assigned.

requirements.title: Keep address rejections out of later assignments
requirements.statement: These address rejections SHOULD NOT be included in subsequent ADDRESS_ASSIGN capsules.

requirements.title: Reject empty address request capsules
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives an ADDRESS_REQUEST capsule that contains zero Requested Addresses, it MUST abort the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Route advertisement capsule format
requirements.statement: A ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT Capsule MUST have Type 0x03, a Length field, and zero or more IP Address Range entries in that order.

requirements.title: IP address range layout
requirements.statement: An IP Address Range MUST contain IP Version (8), Start IP Address (32..128), End IP Address (32..128), and IP Protocol (8) fields in that order.

requirements.title: IP Version field encoding
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: IP Version value constraint
requirements.statement: The IP Version field MUST be either 4 or 6.

requirements.title: IPv4 field length
requirements.statement: When the IP Version field has value 4, the Start IP Address and End IP Address fields MUST have a length of 32 bits.

requirements.title: IPv6 field length
requirements.statement: When the IP Version field has value 6, the Start IP Address and End IP Address fields MUST have a length of 128 bits.

requirements.title: Start address ordering
requirements.statement: The Start IP Address MUST be less than or equal to the End IP Address.

requirements.title: IP Protocol field encoding
requirements.statement: The IP Protocol field MUST be encoded as an unsigned 8-bit integer.

requirements.title: Zero IP Protocol value semantics
requirements.statement: If the IP Protocol field value is 0, all protocols MUST be allowed.

requirements.title: Nonzero IP Protocol values
requirements.statement: If the IP Protocol field value is not 0, it MUST represent an allowable next header value carried in IP headers that are sent directly in HTTP Datagrams (the outermost IP headers).

requirements.title: Always allow ICMP traffic
requirements.statement: ICMP traffic MUST always be allowed, regardless of the IP Protocol field value.

requirements.title: Malformed capsule error handling
requirements.statement: If any of the capsule fields are malformed upon reception, the receiver of the capsule MUST follow the error-handling procedure defined in Section 3.3 of [HTTP-DGRAM].

requirements.title: ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT supersession
requirements.statement: If multiple ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsules are sent in one direction, each ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule MUST supersede prior ones.

requirements.title: Withdrawn range semantics
requirements.statement: If a given address range was present in a prior capsule but the most recently received ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule does not contain it, the receiver MUST consider that range withdrawn.

requirements.title: Order routes by IP Version
requirements.statement: The IP Version of A MUST be less than or equal to the IP Version of B.

requirements.title: Order routes by IP Protocol when versions match
requirements.statement: If the IP Version of A and B are equal, the IP Protocol of A MUST be less than or equal to the IP Protocol of B.

requirements.title: Order route ranges by end and start addresses
requirements.statement: If the IP Version and IP Protocol of A and B are both equal, the End IP Address of A MUST be strictly less than the Start IP Address of B.

requirements.title: Abort invalid ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsules
requirements.statement: If an endpoint receives a ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule that does not meet these requirements, it MUST abort the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Do not send overlapping ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT routes
requirements.statement: Endpoints MUST NOT send a ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule with routes that overlap in such a way.

requirements.title: Abort on detected route violations
requirements.statement: If an endpoint detects the violation, it MUST abort the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Optionally validate ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT routes
requirements.statement: An endpoint MAY validate whether a ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule meets these requirements.

requirements.title: Reject scoping requests for extension-header protocol numbers
requirements.statement: IP proxies MAY reject requests to scope to protocol numbers that are used for extension headers.

requirements.title: Walk extension headers to the outermost non-extension protocol number
requirements.statement: Upon receiving packets, implementations that support scoping or routing by Internet Protocol Number MUST walk the chain of extensions to find the outermost non-extension Internet Protocol Number to match against the scoping rule.

requirements.title: Start HTTP Datagrams with a Context ID field
requirements.statement: HTTP Datagrams associated with IP proxying request streams MUST start with a Context ID field.

requirements.title: Limit Context ID size to 62 bits
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST be 62-bit integers (0 to 2^62-1).

requirements.title: Encode Context IDs as variable-length integers
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST be encoded as variable-length integers.

requirements.title: Allocate non-zero Context IDs dynamically
requirements.statement: Non-zero Context ID values MUST be dynamically allocated.

requirements.title: Reserve Context ID 0 for IP payloads
requirements.statement: The Context ID value of 0 MUST be reserved for IP payloads.

requirements.title: Allow any Context ID allocation order
requirements.statement: Context IDs MAY be allocated in any order.

requirements.title: Disallow Context ID reallocation within a request
requirements.statement: Context IDs MUST NOT be re-allocated within a given HTTP request.

requirements.title: Allow either endpoint to use an allocated Context ID
requirements.statement: Once a Context ID has been allocated, it MAY be used by either the client or the IP proxy, regardless of which endpoint initially allocated it.

requirements.title: Permit future extensions to register Context IDs
requirements.statement: Future extensions MAY use HTTP header fields or capsules to register Context IDs.

requirements.title: Place Context ID after Quarter Stream ID
requirements.statement: When HTTP Datagrams are encoded using QUIC DATAGRAM frames, the Context ID field MUST directly follow the Quarter Stream ID field at the start of the QUIC DATAGRAM frame payload.

requirements.title: Define the IP Proxying HTTP Datagram Payload layout
requirements.statement: The IP Proxying HTTP Datagram Payload MUST consist of a Context ID field followed by a Payload field.

requirements.title: Encode Context ID as a variable-length integer
requirements.statement: The Context ID field MUST be a variable-length integer that contains the value of the Context ID.

requirements.title: Handle unknown Context ID datagrams by dropping or buffering
requirements.statement: If an HTTP/3 datagram carries an unknown Context ID, the receiver SHALL either drop that datagram silently or buffer it temporarily, on the order of a round trip, while awaiting registration of the corresponding Context ID.

requirements.title: Make Payload semantics depend on Context ID
requirements.statement: The semantics of the Payload field MUST depend on the value of the Context ID field.

requirements.title: Allow an empty Payload field
requirements.statement: The Payload field MAY be empty.

requirements.title: Encode IP packets with Context ID zero
requirements.statement: IP packets MUST be encoded using HTTP Datagrams with the Context ID set to zero.

requirements.title: Carry a full IP packet when Context ID is zero
requirements.statement: When the Context ID is set to zero, the Payload field MUST contain a full IP packet from the IP Version field until the last byte of the IP payload.

requirements.title: Allow optimistic proxied IP packet sending
requirements.statement: When using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, a client MAY optimistically start sending proxied IP packets before receiving the response to its IP proxying request.

requirements.title: Process received IP packets from HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: An endpoint that receives an HTTP Datagram containing an IP packet MUST parse the IP header, perform local policy checks, consult its routing table to select an outbound interface, and then send the packet on that interface or pass it to a local application.
notes: Trimmed wording while preserving the single forwarding-path invariant.

requirements.title: Allow additional filtering policies
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints MAY implement additional filtering policies on the IP packets they forward.

requirements.title: Treat failed checks as forwarding errors
requirements.statement: A received IP packet that fails any correctness or policy checks MUST be treated as a forwarding error, not a protocol violation, for IP proxying.

requirements.title: Check routes before sending IP packets over HTTP Datagrams
requirements.statement: When an endpoint receives an IP packet, it MUST check whether it matches routes mapped for an IP tunnel and perform the same forwarding checks as above before transmitting it over HTTP Datagrams.
notes: Trimmed to the smallest standalone routing invariant.

requirements.title: Decrement Hop Count on encapsulation
requirements.statement: When IP proxying endpoints forward IP packets between different links, they MUST decrement the IP Hop Count (or TTL) upon encapsulation.

requirements.title: Do not decrement Hop Count on decapsulation
requirements.statement: When IP proxying endpoints forward IP packets between different links, they MUST not decrement the IP Hop Count (or TTL) upon decapsulation.

requirements.title: Decrement Hop Count before transmission
requirements.statement: The Hop Count of an IP packet MUST be decremented right before the packet is transmitted in an HTTP Datagram.
notes: Kept the timing constraint as its own invariant.

requirements.title: Exclude self-generated packets from hop-count decrement
requirements.statement: The IP Hop Count (or TTL) decrement upon encapsulation MUST not apply to IP packets generated by the IP proxying endpoint itself.
notes: Preserved the exception while trimming the wording to a single normative obligation.

requirements.title: Do not forward link-local traffic beyond the received interface
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints MUST not forward any link-local traffic beyond the IP proxying interface on which it was received.
notes: Retained the negative forwarding constraint as a standalone invariant.

requirements.title: Ensure IPv6 tunnel MTU of at least 1280 bytes
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints that operate as routers and support IPv6 MUST ensure the IP tunnel link MTU is at least 1280 bytes.
notes: Trimmed to the smallest independently testable invariant; meaning preserved.

requirements.title: Use ICMPv6 echo requests to verify link MTU
requirements.statement: Unless endpoints have an out-of-band guarantee that the previous techniques are sufficient, IP proxying endpoints MUST use ICMPv6 echo requests with 1232 bytes of data to determine the link MTU and tear down the tunnel if no response is received.
notes: Trimmed to the actionable invariant while preserving the exception and fallback behavior.

requirements.title: Abort request stream when QUIC MTU is too low
requirements.statement: If an endpoint is using QUIC DATAGRAM frames to convey IPv6 packets and it detects that the QUIC MTU is too low to allow sending 1280 bytes, it MUST abort the IP proxying request stream.

requirements.title: Use ICMP to signal forwarding errors
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints SHOULD signal forwarding errors to their peer by generating ICMP packets and sending them using HTTP Datagrams.
notes: Trimmed explanatory phrasing to the testable forwarding-error signaling invariant.

requirements.title: Send Destination Unreachable for invalid source addresses
requirements.statement: For invalid source addresses, an endpoint SHOULD send Destination Unreachable with ICMPv6 code 5.
notes: Retained the concrete error-code mapping and removed example framing.

requirements.title: Send Destination Unreachable for unroutable destination addresses
requirements.statement: For unroutable destination addresses, an endpoint SHOULD send Destination Unreachable with ICMPv6 code 0 or 1.
notes: Preserves the RFC's allowed choice between the two listed codes.

requirements.title: Send Packet Too Big for MTU-exceeding packets
requirements.statement: For packets that cannot fit within the outgoing-link MTU, an endpoint MUST send Packet Too Big.
notes: Kept only the implementation-relevant MTU-triggered action.

requirements.title: Process proxied ICMP packets when ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT is absent
requirements.statement: If an endpoint does not send ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsules, it SHOULD process proxied ICMP packets from its peer.
notes: Dropped the example and the explanatory receipt clause.

requirements.title: Decrement hop count or TTL when encapsulating forwarded packets
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints MUST decrement the IP Hop Count (or TTL) when encapsulating forwarded packets.

requirements.title: Define new capsule types for configuration exchange
requirements.statement: Extensions SHOULD define new capsule types for configuration exchange when needed.
notes: Trimmed to the smallest independently testable wording.

requirements.title: Avoid burstiness of IP traffic
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints SHOULD avoid increasing burstiness of IP traffic.
notes: Merged with the adjacent burstiness clause in RFC9484-S10-B1-P1-S2; this is the canonical home for the shared invariant.

requirements.title: Avoid extra packet batching
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints SHOULD NOT queue packets to increase batching beyond the minimal amount required to take advantage of hardware offloads.
notes: The shared burstiness clause was merged into RFC9484-S10-B1-P1-S1; this unit retains only the distinct queueing and batching prohibition.

requirements.title: Disable congestion control for DATAGRAM-only packets
requirements.statement: The outer HTTP connection MAY disable congestion control for packets that contain only QUIC DATAGRAM frames encapsulating IP packets.

requirements.title: Prefer HTTP/3 for IP proxying
requirements.statement: IP proxying SHOULD be performed over HTTP/3 to allow leveraging the QUIC DATAGRAM frame.

requirements.title: Transmit IP packets in QUIC DATAGRAM frames
requirements.statement: When using HTTP/3 with the QUIC Datagram extension, IP packets MUST be transmitted in QUIC DATAGRAM frames.

requirements.title: Limit QUIC DATAGRAM frame payload size
requirements.statement: QUIC DATAGRAM frames MUST carry only packets up to the length determined by the QUIC connection configuration and the Path MTU (PMTU).

requirements.title: Avoid DATAGRAM capsules for oversized IP packets
requirements.statement: If an IP packet will not fit inside a QUIC DATAGRAM frame, the IP proxy SHOULD NOT send the IP packet in a DATAGRAM capsule.

requirements.title: Drop oversized IP packets
requirements.statement: When an IP packet will not fit inside a QUIC DATAGRAM frame, the endpoint SHOULD drop the IP packet.

requirements.title: Send Packet Too Big feedback
requirements.statement: When an IP packet will not fit inside a QUIC DATAGRAM frame, the endpoint SHOULD send an ICMP Packet Too Big message to the sender of the dropped packet.

requirements.title: Suppress ECN signaling when congestion control is disabled
requirements.statement: If an IP proxying endpoint with an IP proxying request stream disables congestion control, it MUST NOT signal Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) support on the outer connection.
notes: Trimmed redundant phrasing; no behavior change.

requirements.title: Mark Not-ECT outside congestion control
requirements.statement: The QUIC sender MUST mark all IP headers for QUIC packets outside congestion control with the Not ECN-Capable Transport (Not-ECT) codepoint.
notes: Trimmed wording to the implementation-relevant obligation; no behavior change.

requirements.title: Optionally differentiate traffic by DSCP markings
requirements.statement: If an IP proxying endpoint is configured as part of a Differentiated Services domain, it MAY implement traffic differentiation based on these markings.

requirements.title: Avoid non-equivalent DSCP markings under outer congestion control
requirements.statement: If tunneled packets are subject to congestion control by the outer connection, they MUST NOT carry DSCP markings that are not equivalent in forwarding behavior.

requirements.title: Do not copy inner DSCP values to the outer header
requirements.statement: If tunneled packets are subject to congestion control by the outer connection, the IP proxying endpoint MUST NOT copy the DSCP field from the inner IP header to the outer IP header.
notes: Trimmed redundant trailing wording while preserving the same invariant.

requirements.title: Optionally translate DSCP values for QUIC datagrams
requirements.statement: If tunneled packets use QUIC datagrams and are not subject to congestion control by the outer connection, the IP proxying endpoints MAY translate the DSCP field value from the tunneled traffic to the outer IP header.
notes: Single optional invariant; no wording or trace repair needed.

requirements.title: Do not coalesce inner packets with different DSCP markings
requirements.statement: IP proxying endpoints MUST NOT coalesce multiple inner packets into the same outer packet unless they have the same DSCP marking or an equivalent traffic class.
notes: Single required invariant; wording already minimal.

requirements.title: Restrict IP proxying to authenticated users
requirements.statement: HTTP servers that support IP proxying SHOULD restrict its use to authenticated users.

requirements.title: Avoid persistent per-client address assignment
requirements.statement: Proxies SHOULD avoid persistent per-client address (prefix) assignment when possible.

requirements.title: Follow BCP38 to prevent source address spoofing
requirements.statement: In such scenarios, endpoints MUST follow the recommendations from [BCP38] to prevent source address spoofing.

requirements.title: Optionally forward ICMP packets to clients
requirements.statement: If the proxy receives an ICMP packet destined for that external IP address, it MAY forward it to the clients.

requirements.title: Filter ICMP forwarding by invoking packet scope
requirements.statement: Proxies that forward ICMP on shared external IP addresses MUST forward each ICMP packet only to the client whose scoping matches the invoking packet.
notes: Trimmed to the smallest forwarding rule while preserving the scope-match check.

requirements.title: Prohibit opportunistic sending of IP packets in HTTP/1.x
requirements.statement: Opportunistic sending of IP packets MUST NOT be used in HTTP/1.x.

requirements.title: Delay capsules until a successful IP proxying response
requirements.statement: An intermediary that re-encodes a request from HTTP/2 or 3 to HTTP/1.1 MUST NOT forward any received capsules until it has parsed a successful IP proxying response.
notes: Kept the forwarding gate and tightened the phrasing for canonical use.

requirements.title: Require Expert Review registration policy
requirements.statement: The MASQUE URI Suffixes registry MUST use the Expert Review registration policy.

requirements.title: Constrain registry path segments to token characters
requirements.statement: Registry Path Segment values MUST be ASCII strings containing only token characters.

requirements.title: Require distinct registry path segments
requirements.statement: Entries in this registry MUST have distinct Path Segment values.

requirements.title: Guide expert approval for MASQUE URI suffix requests
requirements.statement: Designated experts SHOULD approve requests when the requested Path Segment will not conflict with existing or expected future IETF work and the use case is relevant to proxying.
